title: Nadir Shah's forgotten comedian: the jester who mocked an empire
hook: Discover how a daring court jester became the unlikely nadir shah comedian who mocked royalty.
description:
A hidden comic in Nadir Shah's court turned satire into a weapon that rattled empires.

Subscribe for more untold history.

beats.say: In 1730 Tehran welcomed the birth of Jafar Qoli, a quick-wit from a modest merchant family.
By 1738 he entered Nadir Shah's court, juggling jokes as the sultan's nervous eyes watched.
His favorite target was the feared commander Mashhour, whom he mocked for fearing his own shadow.
During the 1740 campaign in Kandahar, Jafar slipped a satirical verse onto a soldier's drum, sparking laughter amidst gunfire.
The sultan, amused yet uneasy, granted Jafar a golden mask, branding him the 'Laughing Blade'.
When Nadir Shah demanded tribute from the Mughal governor, Jafar whispered a parody song that mocked the tax collector's greed.
The parody spread through the army, turning the grim march into a chorus of chuckles, unsettling rival generals.
In 1745, Jafar's satire reached the Ottoman envoy, who laughed so hard he signed a peace draft with a doodle.
Nadir Shah, fearing ridicule, ordered Jafar's exile, but the jester escaped to the mountains, becoming a folk legend.
Decades later, his verses resurfaced in bazaars, reminding Iranians that even tyrants tremble before laughter.
